target_customer: AI labs, university research teams, industrial operators and event producers that need robots, parts and robot data fast
problem: Teams building physical AI struggle to buy robots and parts quickly in the US and to collect teleoperation data and deploy robots.
business_model: Hardware resale plus services (data collection, deployment) and a data marketplace
product_category: Robotics hardware distribution and physical AI data services

founders.name: Jerry Huang
previous_startups: Earlier company providing second-level energy optimization to dozens of factories (outcome not stated)
founders.background_notes: YC page says both founders are second-time founders who spent three years on the previous company.

founders.name: Stela Tong
previous_startups: Same earlier energy optimization company (outcome not stated)

technical_complexity.rationale: Reselling and supporting third party robots (Unitree, OpenArm) and collecting data is operationally demanding but not research grade.

defensibility.rationale: Hardware reselling has thin margins and little lock-in; a teleoperation dataset library (20k+ hours claimed) and community of 1200+ members could add some advantage.

market_need_then: Demand for humanoid and arm hardware and robot learning data rose with the 2025 physical AI wave; no company specific demand evidence beyond the site's claim of university customers.

branding.domain_note: Operates on roboticscenter.ai rather than a DeepAware domain.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and practical: 'Robotics Hardware & Data in 48 hours' (company site)

rebrands.why: Not stated; YC page notes an older launch post about RL for data center energy.

branding.community_and_virality: Site cites monthly community meetups and 1200+ members (self reported).

brand_strength.rationale: Two names in use, the new one is generic and resembles other Silicon Valley robotics groups; no press about the brand.

pivots.from: RL based automation for data center energy management (YC launch post)
pivots.to: Robots, parts, RL environments and data sold from the Robotics Center of Silicon Valley

outcome_analysis: DeepAware joined YC S25 with a data center energy product and now operates mainly as a robotics hardware and data seller under the Robotics Center of Silicon Valley name. Funding is unclear beyond an unverified roughly 500K total, there is no exit, and the business is active with open job listings, so the story is an early pivot into physical AI supply with no confirmed traction metrics.
notes: Funding unverified: Dealroom says $500K in January 2025 from Augur VC, Exitfund and Nvidia; ZeroG Talent says a seed in September 2025 with 2 unnamed investors; the company site says it is backed by YC (S25) and NVIDIA Inception, a program rather than a round. No round recorded. Founder education and employers not on any source opened. No dated competitor near the batch was found, so the list is empty (RobotShop appeared but with no dated source). The 'DeepAware' name is also used for the older data center product.
